name: Knowledge commons
definition: A shared knowledge resource system whose community, rules, resource characteristics, interactions, and outcomes can be analyzed together.

name: Information commons
definition: An information resource or environment organized for shared access, use, contribution, or stewardship.

name: Intellectual commons
definition: A shared domain for the creation, exchange, and reuse of intellectual work.

name: Scholarly communication commons
definition: Shared infrastructures, norms, repositories, and publication systems for scholarly communication.

name: Digital commons
definition: A commons whose resources, access facilities, and participation are substantially digital and networked.

name: Open-access commons
definition: A knowledge commons organized around free online access and permissions broad enough for scholarly use.

name: Scientific or research commons
definition: Shared scientific literature, data, models, tools, or collaborative infrastructure supporting research.

name: Cultural commons
definition: Shared cultural works, heritage materials, archives, and the institutions or rules sustaining access to them.

name: Civic knowledge commons
definition: A participatory civic resource through which residents, students, or organizations create and use public knowledge.

name: Learning commons
definition: A shared educational environment combining information resources, technology, instruction, and collaborative learning.

name: Community information commons
definition: A community-facing information environment that supports local access, deliberation, contribution, and public problem solving.

name: Digital library
definition: A managed digital collection with discovery, access, organization, and often preservation services.

name: Digital archive
definition: A managed body of digital objects maintained across time with provenance, authenticity, or preservation responsibilities.

name: Institutional repository
definition: A repository organized by an institution to collect, expose, and often preserve its community's scholarly output.

name: Disciplinary repository
definition: A repository organized around a discipline or research community rather than one institution.

name: Epistemic repository
definition: A repository designed around a community's structured knowledge, concepts, evidence, and reusable research objects.

name: Specialist archive
definition: A focused archive built for a specialist scholarly field, corpus, format, or community.

name: Community-based archive
definition: An archive shaped and maintained with direct participation by the community represented in its holdings.

name: Author self-archive
definition: A repository or site through which authors deposit and expose their own work.

name: Open educational resource library
definition: A collection or gateway providing openly accessible teaching and learning materials.

name: Searchable portal
definition: A central discovery interface that searches or organizes resources held locally and elsewhere.

name: Annotated link gateway
definition: A link-only gateway that points to off-site resources and adds classification metadata and descriptive context.

name: Metadata aggregation or harvesting service
definition: A service that collects standardized metadata from distributed repositories to support shared discovery.

name: Directory or registry
definition: A structured listing of projects, repositories, policies, people, resources, or implementations.

name: Open-access journal
definition: A journal that makes its articles freely accessible online under an open-access delivery model.

name: Open publication platform
definition: A shared service for publishing, reviewing, distributing, or linking scholarly works outside a conventional closed journal system.

name: Free/libre and open-source software commons
definition: A software project whose code, participation rules, licenses, and collaborative production constitute a commons.

name: Open-content science commons
definition: A proposed or operating science commons applying open-source participation, review, licensing, and versioning to scientific content.

name: Scientific data commons
definition: Shared infrastructure for depositing, accessing, documenting, and reusing scientific datasets.

name: Collaboratory
definition: A networked environment in which geographically distributed participants share data, instruments, tools, and research work.

name: Information community
definition: A community joined by shared information practices, resources, tools, standards, and stewardship.

name: Federated or distributed library
definition: Multiple independent repositories or institutions connected through shared protocols, services, or discovery layers.

name: Coalition or membership network
definition: A network of institutions or projects coordinating access, policy, preservation, standards, or advocacy.

name: Organizational archive
definition: An archive housed within the same organization as either the producer or consumer, or contracted to a third party.

name: Producer archive
definition: An archive maintained by the organization or person producing the content.

name: Consumer archive
definition: An archive maintained by the institution or community consuming and relying on the content.

name: Independent third-party archive
definition: A preservation archive institutionally separate from both producer and consumer.

name: Distributed preservation network
definition: A preservation arrangement using redundant, distributed copies or caches across participating institutions.

name: Dark archive or fallback-access archive
definition: A preservation service whose stored materials become accessible only under defined loss, trigger, or continuity conditions.

name: Open licensing infrastructure
definition: Licenses, registries, declarations, or policy services that define reusable permissions for knowledge resources.

name: Standards and interoperability infrastructure
definition: Shared metadata, identifiers, protocols, interfaces, and technical rules that let independent commons interoperate.

name: Traditional natural-resource commons
definition: Shared forests, fisheries, pastures, water systems, and other subtractable resources used as the analytical starting point for knowledge commons.

name: Public domain
directoryRole: Legal status and surrounding resource pool
definition: Knowledge and cultural material available outside exclusive copyright control, serving as a key resource environment for commons projects.
